extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing interim suspension of a patent practitioner under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, including notice, opportunity to respond, referral to a hearing officer, and post-suspension obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for interim suspension (conviction of serious crime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be ordered predicated on evidence that Respondent committed a serious crime, which was a felony offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order here was issued because Respondent was found guilty of Possession of Methamphetamine, a Class 2 Felony (720 ILCS 646/60(a) and (b)(2)), and action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority for interim suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings and interim suspension are authorized by 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25; referrals and further disciplinary proceedings follow 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to the statutory and regulatory provisions set the framework for issuing notice, imposing interim suspension, limited recognition, and referral to a hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and method of service
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25' must be sent to the Respondent (here by certified mail) and delivered to afford opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document notes certified mail with receipt numbers and states that the Notice and Order was delivered to Respondent on a specific date; factual proof of mailing/delivery is used to establish notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond (40-day response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a response within the 40-day period is consequential (see 'Failure to respond' criterion). The Notice and Order explicitly provided this 40-day window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Respondent does not file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 and find interim suspension appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states that in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, an interim suspension is appropriate because there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension effective immediately and limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended on an interim basis effective the date of the Final Order; limited recognition to practice is granted commencing on the date of the Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Order is signed, solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is temporary and narrowly tailored for compliance purposes; suspension otherwise restricts practice in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint shall be referred to a hearing officer (here at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development) for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates the formal adjudicative process following interim suspension; the Complaint copy is attached and transmitted as required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer to the Complaint (30-day deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.36, Respondent's written answer to the Complaint must be filed with the hearing officer within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies mailing and hand-delivery addresses for the Docket Clerk at the HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals and requires that a PDF version of the answer be filed via email with the hearing office and that a copy be served on the OED Director by mail (Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service procedures for responses/answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers must be filed at specified addresses (postal and hand-delivery) and an electronic PDF must be emailed to the hearing office; a copy must be served on the OED Director by mail to the designated USPTO address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides explicit contact details for mail and hand-delivery and requires both physical filing and PDF email submission plus service on OED, establishing formal service and filing protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a 'Notice of Interim Suspension' in the Official Gazette describing the Respondent, registration number, the interim suspension, the underlying conviction, and citations to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must include the practitioner's name, registration number, state conviction details, and a reference to where disciplinary decisions are publicly available (OED FOIA Reading Room URL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication and identifies the FOIA reading room as the public repository for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to relevant authorities and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to appropriate USPTO employees; interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures interagency and state bar notification of interim disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with post-suspension duties (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, which governs practitioner obligations upon suspension (e.g., notification of clients, transfer of files, and other duties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition granted for 30 days is specifically to facilitate Respondent's compliance with § 11.58(b); the Order reiterates the duty to comply with § 11.58 generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative action severs the practitioner's access and association with USPTO electronic/customer accounts while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or associating with Customer Numbers while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall his name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents circumvention of suspension via third-party or new customer numbers until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of seeking review on suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenging the suspension administratively or otherwise does not stay the suspension; suspension remains in effect during review.
